lines: What if all the air on Earth vanished for just five seconds?
First, total silence. Sound needs air to travel.
The sky turns black. That blue was just sunlight bouncing off air.
Your ears pop, and the spit on your tongue starts to boil.
Planes and birds lose their lift and drop. Fires go out.
Myth: your body explodes. Nope. Your skin holds it all together.
You stay awake for about ten seconds. A NASA tester made fourteen, in nineteen sixty-five.
Then the air slams back in with a huge boom. Never hold your breath. Your lungs can rupture.
So, would you hold it, or breathe out?
